powerOfPlay.title: Discover the power of play
powerOfPlay.subtitle: Play engages both mind and body, making learning an active, immersive experience.
powerOfPlay.intro: Welcome to #play14, a global movement that believes in the transformative power of play! We are a worldwide gathering of like-minded people who believe that playing is the best way to learn, share and foster creativity!
powerOfPlay.body: Through play, individuals explore, experiment, and discover concepts in a hands-on way, which enhances understanding and retention. Playfulness encourages innovation, problem-solving, and collaboration, helping learners develop critical thinking skills.
powerOfPlay.quote: Tell me and I forget, teach me and I may remember, involve me and I learn
powerOfPlay.conclusion: Play also reduces stress and increases motivation, making the learning process enjoyable and effective. By creating a safe space for trial and error, play fosters a deeper, more meaningful connection to the material being learned.

joinMovement.title: Join the movement
joinMovement.subtitle: Join us in cities worldwide to connect with like-minded individuals.
joinMovement.intro: Whether you are a facilitator, educator, or curious mind, our events are designed to spark creativity, foster collaboration, and ignite new ideas. Dive into a world of playful experimentation.
joinMovement.globalCommunity: Global community: Connect with a diverse network of innovators.
joinMovement.endlessFun: Endless fun: Engage in hands-on, playful activities.
joinMovement.inspire: Inspire & be inspired: Share and discover new games, tools, and techniques.
joinMovement.unconference: #play14 is an unconference, where all attendees are also contributors. Just show up with an open mind, and you'll have the chance to propose your own games or dive into the games suggested by others. It's all about participation, creativity, and shared fun!

experience.title: The experience
experience.subtitle: For two and a half days, people with many different profiles share games and activities, knowledge, and laughs. Everyone is welcome.
experience.activitiesIntro: Here are some examples of activities we engage in:
experience.seriousGame: A <link>serious game</link> that you use as a metaphor in order to understand a new concept
experience.iceBreaker: An <link>ice breaker</link> game where people learn more about one another
experience.warmUp: A <warmup>warm up</warmup> or an <energizer>energizer</energizer> that you can use to raise the level of awareness and energy
experience.facilitation: A facilitation technique that you can use in your daily work
experience.teamBuilding: A <link>team building</link> exercise that fosters collaboration and self organization
experience.gameDesign: A <link>game design</link> session where you invent a new game to teach something new
experience.soulSearching: A soul searching, deep-dive introspection session where you learn about yourself
experience.coaching: A one-on-one coaching session where you will find some answers with the help of a friend
experience.brainstorming: A brainstorming session on a question or problem that wakes you up at night
experience.creative: A <link>creative session</link> where you sketch, doodle, or build something together
experience.funTime: A fun and energetic time with <dancing>dancing</dancing>, <singing>singing</singing> or being silly together
experience.improv: An <link>improv theater</link> session where you can work on your confidence and ability to speak publicly
experience.esoteric: A more esoteric session on a practice/hobby you want to share like yoga, laughter yoga, Tai Chi, Qigong, meditation, mindfulness, aikido, ...
experience.callToAction: Join us in order to develop your facilitation skills, increase your ability to accompany change in your organization, foster your creativity and improve your capacity to innovate.
experience.quote: You can discover more about a person in an hour of play than a year of conversation

eventDuration.question: How long does an event last?
eventDuration.answer: A typical #play14 event lasts 2.5 days on average. Events usually start on Friday afternoon or evening and end on Sunday afternoon. This format allows participants to fully immerse themselves in the experience while still having time to travel.

unconference.question: What is an unconference?
unconference.answer: An unconference is a participant-driven event where attendees are also contributors. #play14 follows the Open Space Technology format, meaning there is no predefined agenda. Instead, participants propose games and activities each morning during the marketplace session, and the schedule emerges organically.

proposeGame.question: Do I need to propose a game to attend?
proposeGame.answer: No, not at all! It's perfectly fine to attend #play14 without proposing any game or activity. You can simply participate in sessions proposed by others. However, if you discover a game you love, you might feel inspired to facilitate it at a future event!

lawOfTwoFeet.question: What is the Law of Two Feet?
lawOfTwoFeet.answer: The Law of Two Feet is a core principle of Open Space Technology. It means that if you find yourself in a session where you are neither learning nor contributing, you have the responsibility to use your two feet and move somewhere else. Neither the facilitator nor other participants should feel offended — it's simply how the format works.

whoCanAttend.question: Who can attend #play14?
whoCanAttend.answer: Everyone is welcome! Our community includes facilitators, agile coaches, educators, trainers, HR professionals, team leaders, and curious minds from all backgrounds. Whether you're experienced with serious games or completely new to the concept, you'll find your place at #play14.

commercial.question: Is #play14 a commercial event?
commercial.answer: No, #play14 is non-profit. We are a community-driven movement focused on sharing knowledge and practices rather than selling services. Event fees cover venue rental, food, and materials. Any surplus is reinvested into future events or the community.

activities.question: What kind of activities can I expect?
activities.answer: You can expect a wide variety of activities including serious games that teach concepts through play, ice breakers to get to know each other, energizers to boost the group's energy, team building exercises, facilitation techniques, creative sessions, improv theater, and even more esoteric activities like yoga or meditation. The beauty of an unconference is that anything can happen!

experience.question: Do I need prior experience with games or facilitation?
experience.answer: No prior experience is needed. #play14 welcomes beginners and experts alike. Many participants discover new games at their first event and return to facilitate those same games later. The community is supportive and everyone learns from each other, regardless of experience level.

codeOfConduct.title: Code of conduct
codeOfConduct.openMinded: You shall be open minded and ready to listen and learn from others
codeOfConduct.propose: You shall feel free to propose, experiment and explain what you have in mind
codeOfConduct.noHighjack: You shall not high-jack, sabotage or ruin the learning experience of others
codeOfConduct.timebox: You shall manage your own timebox when facilitating so that other sessions can start on time
codeOfConduct.behave: You shall behave appropriately and be a decent human being
codeOfConduct.clean: You shall always leave the playground clean (boy scout rule), avoid waste and try to reduce your carbon footprint
codeOfConduct.fun: You shall be ready to get serious fun and good laughs and should try not be shy about that
codeOfConduct.summary: To summarize: “You shall not be an a**hole”.

values.title: Our values
values.intro: Values are very important to us. They are what make #play14 what it is. Please, make sure you take a look at our manifesto and our code of conduct before you register to one of our events.
values.thanksNina: Many thanks to <link>Nina Neef</link> for the wonderful images.
values.scoutSaying: Always leave the campground cleaner than you found it.
values.scoutText1: Be mindful of other people well being by cleaning after yourself when you leave a space. That goes for the space you played on, the space you ate on, the space you rested on, etc.
values.scoutText2: Remember that the hosting team is not there to clean after you, but are also participants of the event. They also want to facilitate and attend sessions, as much as you do.

format.title: Our format
format.unconferenceIntro: #play14 is organized as an unconference, a conference format that follows the <link>Open Space Technology</link>
format.unconferenceContributors: In this format, attendees are also session contributors. Anyone who wants to initiate a topic can claim a time slot in the agenda, and the schedule is done every morning, on the spot, as we will explain later.
format.unconferenceParticipant: Once you are there, the organizers' job is over. They have provided a location, food, and drinks for the rest of the event, then it's up to you as a participant to make it a great event.
format.funnyDrawings: Check out the <drawings>funny drawings</drawings> of <author>Claudio Perrone</author>
format.principlesIntro: There are some simple rules for participants.
format.whoeverComes: Whoever comes is the right people
format.whoeverComesText: As a facilitator, you should welcome anyone who has decided to join your session, and not be frustrated if you expected different people. As a participant, you should be ready to collaborate with anyone.
format.wheneverStarts: Whenever it starts is the right time
format.wheneverStartsText: As a facilitator, if you need some time to prepare, take it. Just think that people might get bored and go join another session. The best is to prepare anything in advance. As a participant, there is nothing wrong with joining a session in progress. But respect the people who have already started, and try to jump in quietly.
format.whereverItIs: Wherever it is, is the right place
format.whereverItIsText: You will be offered several spaces for your session. Choose the one that fits your needs as a facilitator or as a participant.
format.whateverHappens: Whatever happens, is the only thing that could have
format.whateverHappensText: Be prepared to be surprised. Don't be annoyed if you get feedback. Don't be disappointed if it doesn't work. Try again if need be.
format.whenItsOverText: As a facilitator, it's up to you to mind your timebox. The organizers will not do it for you. Keep in mind that the participants of your session might want to go to another session after yours and that the room might be reserved after. Feel free to continue in a different location with whoever is interested.
format.lawOfTwoFeetText: Any time a person feels a session is not contributing to their learning, they have the responsibility to themselves to get up and move. That is, use their two feet or four wheels to move to a more interesting place. Neither the facilitator nor the other participants should feel offended about that. It's just what it is.
format.butterflyText: A butterfly sits around looking relaxed and interesting discussions may emerge around them as people find them and pause to chat.
format.bumblebeeText: A bumblebee flies from one group to the other and cross-pollinating the discussions.
format.howSchedule: How does the schedule come up?
format.scheduleIntro: #play14 being an unconference, it's up to the participants to come up with the schedule. This is done every morning after some warm-up games when we fill up the marketplace.
format.marketplaceExplain: The marketplace is a large board where you find vertically the list of all the spaces/rooms available, and horizontally all the time slots during the day. The participants come up with the schedule by adding their game/activity to the board.
format.howPropose: How do I propose a game?
format.proposeIntro: If you feel like proposing a game, you will have to pitch it in front of everyone, and then add it to the marketplace.
format.proposeSteps: In order to do that, you need to:
format.proposeStep2: Write down the name of your game/activity. You can also draw something.
format.proposeStep3: Add the minimum and maximum number of people you need, and the time the game will approximately last.
format.proposeStep4: Add your name so we know who the sticky belongs to
format.proposeStep5: Enter the queue and pitch your game to the audience
format.proposeStep6: Pick a time slot and room on the marketplace and stick your sticky note
format.proposeDetails: You do not need to go into many details. Just explain the main concept of your game, and list some of the takeaways. The goal is to give enough information so that people want to come to your session.
format.proposeKeepShort: To keep it fun, make sure to keep it short.
format.notNewGame: What if the game I propose is not new?
format.notNewGameText1: It is perfectly fine to propose that has already been proposed by someone else or played before. Actually, it is encouraged, if you want to get better at facilitating. Over the years, some games have become the #play14 classics. Facilitating one of these is a great way to progress.
format.notNewGameText2: Remember that #play14 is about experimenting. It is by taking some risks and getting out of your comfort zone that you will get better. We have seen people who discovered a game one day as a player and facilitated that same game the next day.
format.shouldDebrief: Should I plan on debriefing my game?
format.shouldDebriefText1: YES, YES, and again YES. There is nothing sadder than a great game, full of learning opportunities, without a good debrief. Always keep some time to debrief your game/activity at the end of your session. It's your responsibility as a facilitator to make sure that all the participants can learn as much as possible from your game.
format.shouldDebriefText2: Remember that debriefing is about asking questions, not explaining to people what they should feel or understand. Try not to project your own understanding of the game, but instead ask powerful questions that will lead the group to insights linked to their own experience.
format.shouldDebriefText3: A great tool to help you do that is <link>The Debriefing Cube</link>.
format.noGame: What if I don't have any game/activity to propose?
format.noGameItem1: It's perfectly fine to attend #play14 without proposing any game/activity.
format.noGameItem2: Just make sure you get the most out of your days by participating the the games/activities you are most interested in
format.noGameItem3: Use the law of two feet if you don't get enough value out of the session or think you can make yourself useful elsewhere
format.noGameItem4: Next time you attend, maybe you will have some game/activity to share
format.whatMaterial: What kind of material will be available?
format.materialIntro: Common workshop materials and stationery will be available.
format.materialSpecific: If your game requires specific material, make sure you bring it with you or ask the hosting team in advance. If you cannot find what you are looking for, feel free to improvise.
format.whatElse: What else do I need to know?
format.whatElseIntro: Here is what you need to know when attending a #play14 event.
